verdict.rationale: New Relic's own service level management docs say users can define SLIs and SLOs, from one-click to fully customizable advanced modes, and its alerting platform supports threshold and anomaly conditions. However, nothing in the evidence documents error budgets or burn-rate alerting tied to SLOs, and generic threshold alerts cannot be credited as burn-rate alerts. Missing for 10: documented error budget tracking, documented SLO burn-rate alert conditions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can define SLOs with error budgets and burn-rate alerts

citations.quote: With New Relic, you can define and consume service level indicators (SLIs) and service level objectives (SLOs) for your applications.
facilitates creation of service levels with different modes of complexity, from one-click to advanced modes fully customizable for advanced users.
Configure any signal to be evaluated against a threshold, or if it exhibits abnormal behavior.
